---

### **Bubble Sort Time Complexity**

| Case | Explanation | Time Complexity |
|------|-------------|----------------|
| **Best Case** | Array already sorted → just one pass, no swaps | **O(n)** |
| **Average Case** | Random order → many comparisons & some swaps | **O(n²)** |
| **Worst Case** | Reverse sorted → max comparisons & swaps | **O(n²)** |

---

### **Space Complexity**
- Uses only a few extra variables → **O(1)** (constant space)

---

### Short reason (if asked)
> Bubble sort compares each pair repeatedly. That gives n passes and (n − 1) comparisons per pass → **n × (n − 1) ≈ n²**.

---

### **Time Complexity — Normal Bubble Sort**

| Case | Why | Complexity |
|------|-----|------------|
| **Best Case** | Even if already sorted, it still does all passes and all comparisons | **O(n²)** |
| **Average Case** | Random data → full passes, many swaps | **O(n²)** |
| **Worst Case** | Reverse sorted → maximum comparisons + swaps | **O(n²)** |

---

### **Space Complexity**
- Only temporary variable for swapping → **O(1)**

---

### **Short Explanation (one-liner for exam)**  
> Normal bubble sort always performs n passes and (n−1) comparisons in each pass → (n × n) → **O(n²)** in all cases.
